question.text: Per NISM Section 1.4.1, the real risk-free rate in an economy is determined by the INTERACTION of which of the following factors?

answer.text: Central bank policy rate and commercial bank MCLR spread only.
Subjective factor of desire for current consumption AND objective factors of available investment opportunities and the real growth rate of the economy.
Inflation expectations and central bank inflation targeting band.
Equity risk premium and sovereign credit default swap spreads.

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 1.4.1 explicitly states: 'the real risk-free rate is determined by an interaction between subjective factors like the desire for consumption and objective factors like the available investment opportunities and the growth rate of the economy.' This is the chapter's definition verbatim. The Trap: Option A conflates real risk-free rate with monetary-policy instruments. Option C mixes real with inflation — the two are distinct legs of the Fisher decomposition. Option D describes risk-premium inputs, not real-rate inputs. Note: The Chapter 1 determinants are subjective (desire for current consumption) and objective (available investment opportunities and the real growth rate of the economy); these together drive the real risk-free rate.
